rules.name: Notice Period Before Adverse Action
rules.description: Examines the elapsed time between the notice recorded in the case file and the adverse action that followed it.
rules.authority: California Legislature / County Board of Supervisors
rules.notes: UNVERIFIED DAY COUNT. § 25845 requires a reasonable opportunity to correct but the operative period depends on the abatement track and on Humboldt County Code chapter 352, which may specify a shorter local period. The 30-day figure is carried over from the project's own statute library and must be confirmed against the controlling section before this rule is activated. Abatement and lien events are deliberately excluded here because HCC 352-4(c) and 352-23 govern those intervals specifically; a general and a specific rule reporting different periods on the same fact misleads the reader.

rules.name: Opportunity To Be Heard Before Deprivation
rules.description: Examines whether the record contains a hearing or contest opportunity preceding an adverse action affecting the property.
rules.citation: Mathews v. Eldridge (1976) 424 U.S. 319; Goldberg v. Kelly (1970) 397 U.S. 254
rules.notes: Constitutional baseline, not a statutory deadline. Mathews supplies the balancing test for what process is due; it does not itself fix a required form of hearing for county code enforcement. Whether a pre-deprivation hearing was constitutionally required in a given matter is a legal question for counsel, not for this checkpoint.

rules.name: Appeal Rights Disclosed In Decision
rules.description: Examines whether a decision document in the case file states how the recipient may seek review.
rules.citation: Mullane v. Central Hanover Bank & Trust Co. (1950) 339 U.S. 306
rules.notes: Mullane governs the adequacy of notice generally. It does not hold that every administrative decision must recite appeal rights; many California agencies carry that duty by statute or ordinance instead. Confirm the local source before treating an absent disclosure as significant.

rules.name: Abatement Following Notice Of Violation
rules.description: Examines the elapsed time between a recorded notice of violation and a recorded abatement of the property.
rules.notes: Carried over from the FairProcess policy pack, where the reviewed text of HCC § 352-4(c) established an earliest date of 10 days after service but no explicit latest date. Summary abatement of an imminent hazard proceeds on a different track and this checkpoint does not distinguish it.

rules.name: Administrative Penalty Lien Recordation
rules.description: Examines the elapsed time between service and the recordation of an administrative civil penalty lien.
rules.notes: The reviewed text indicates the lien has force and effect only upon recordation. Confirm the currently codified text before activation — this section has been amended.

rules.name: Review Opportunity After Permit Denial
rules.description: Examines whether the record contains a review or appeal opportunity following a permit denial or expiration.
rules.citation: Cal. Gov. Code § 65010; Humboldt County Code § 312-1
rules.authority: California Legislature / Humboldt County Planning Division
rules.notes: UNVERIFIED. The controlling appeal pathway for a Humboldt permit denial depends on which body issued the denial and is not established by § 65010 alone. This checkpoint reports only what the case file contains and should not be read as asserting an appeal was owed.

rules.name: Case Closure With Review On Record
rules.description: Examines whether a closed code enforcement case shows a hearing or appeal in the record before closure.
rules.authority: California Legislature / County Board of Supervisors
rules.notes: Informational only. Many cases close by voluntary compliance, where no hearing is expected or required. A result here is a prompt to look, not a signal of irregularity.

rules.name: Public Records Act Response Timing
rules.description: Examines the elapsed time between a public records request and the agency's response.
rules.notes: UNVERIFIED DAY COUNT. The Public Records Act generally requires a response within 10 calendar days of a request, with a further 14-day extension available in writing for specified reasons (unusual circumstances: the request seeks records from multiple facilities, requires search through a large volume of records, requires consultation with another agency, or requires computer programming to extract data) under Gov. Code § 7922.545. This rule uses the base 10-day figure and does not currently model the extension. IMPORTANT: this rule's evaluator (used for the findings panel) only fires once a response event exists to measure the interval against -- if no response has been logged at all, it correctly reports AwaitingTrigger, which means only 'no response event is logged yet', NOT 'the county is not yet overdue.' For a request where the window may already be blown with no response received, the Deadline Bar (not this findings panel) is the correct place to see how many days overdue the county is -- it compares the request date directly against today, independent of whether a response was ever logged. A verbal promise to send records, if made, is not itself a response under the Act and does not extend the statutory window -- confirm this reading with counsel before relying on it.
